human_review: Network traffic and DNS

AI usage and retries

Whether a flagged sign-in or role is legitimate before any account is blocked or role removed; the identity owner makes every change.

Each client's settings and export mapping, and every client-facing note before it is sent.

reaches_the_model: A Fairwire tool reads the exported file on your own computer and returns a summary and a list of findings. Before that result leaves the computer, names, sign-in names, e-mail addresses, phone numbers, IMEIs and the public addresses people connected from are replaced with stable pseudonyms (16 of the 31 agents read such fields; of 262 personal values in the test files, none reached the model). Dates, counts, amounts, codes, device names and internal addresses are sent in clear; strict mode also masks host names and every address. Free-text fields such as rule descriptions or ticket titles are scrubbed of e-mail addresses, phone numbers and names seen elsewhere in the file, but other personal details typed into them can get through. The result goes to whichever AI model your assistant uses; for regulated data, use a local model or one covered by your own agreements.
rules_maintained: Thresholds such as days to patch, retention days, SLA targets, call-quality limits and the top-admin cap are working defaults in each agent's settings, and a customer changes them in a settings file without touching code. Facts that come from vendors are dated and kept in one place, fairwire-core: the Windows end-of-support list (as of 19 Nov 2026, checked against endoflife.date), risky inbound ports, cleartext protocols, cloud host names used for takeover checks, and the 14 vendor export layouts the agents recognise. A customer can override each of them in settings or in fairwire-sources.json; Mythos Machines updates the defaults in new releases, and support covers export layouts that a vendor changes.
